newsitem.title: USA: Houseboat owner in Versace case may be fugitive.
newsitem.headline: Houseboat owner in Versace case may be fugitive.

text.p: German police said on Thursday they believed the owner of a houseboat where fashion designer Gianni Versace's alleged killer was found dead may be a fugitive they have been seeking since 1992.

A spokesman for police in the eastern city of Leipzig confirmed they were looking for Torsten Reineck, a man named in U.S. media reports as the owner of the houseboat where police found Andrew Cunanan dead in an apparent suicide on Wednesday.

The spokesman told Reuters Reineck was wanted on charges of fraud and tax evasion over two Leipzig businesses he set up. The companies, a marketing firm and a real estate company, later went bankrupt and Reineck went missing.
The spokesman said a European arrest warrant had been issued against Reineck on those charges. A total of 37 charges relating to his business dealings were outstanding, he added.
Asked if police believed the houseboat owner was also the man they were looking for, the spokesman said: "It's speculative but we assume so. It would fit."
The notion that Reineck may be in the United States seemed likely as a European arrest warrant had been issued against him, the police spokesman said.
Local television in Miami said Reineck, a German national, also owned a gay health club in Las Vegas. Police described Cunanan as a homosexual prostitute.
Versace was also a homosexual, but there was no confirmation the fashion designer had had a relationship with Cunanan.
A spokesman at the Germany's Federal Office for Criminal Investigation (BKA) said the European warrant against Reineck had been issued in 1993.
He said U.S. investigators had not yet asked for more information about Reineck as far as he knew.
German regional crime investigators said it was likely the German authorities would be in touch with their U.S. counterparts for details about Reineck.
"Normally in a case like this, when information about the whereabouts of someone on an international arrest warrant appears, a request for details would follow," a spokesman said.

Versace was shot and killed on July 15 at the gate of his oceanfront mansion in the South Beach area of Miami Beach, about two miles (3 km) south of the houseboat's mooring. Cunanan was the prime suspect in the police investigation.
